standard.title: Family structures and roles over time
standard.description: differences in family structures and roles today, and how these have changed or remained the same over time
standard.prior_knowledge: From Foundation (AC9HSFK01): Students identified people in their family, where they were born and raised, and how family members are related. They used relationship vocabulary and created concept maps of family.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain differences in family structures and roles today, and describe how these have changed or remained the same over time.

nodes.label: Variety of family structures today
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify a range of family structures in contemporary Australia and describe how they differ from each other.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three different family structures (e.g. nuclear, single-parent, extended, blended) and describe one way they differ.
nodes.typical_width: Explore the full range of family structures including nuclear, one-child, large, single-parent, extended, blended/step, adoptive, foster, grandparent-led and kinship group families; describe similarities and differences between them.
wider: Investigate kinship group structures in First Nations Australian communities and compare with Western family structure categories
Explore how families in different countries are structured differently and what shapes those structures
nodes.hinge_reason: Without understanding the range of current family structures, students cannot compare them with past structures — the baseline comparison requires knowing what the current variety looks like.

response_modes.reason: Students need exposure to a genuinely wide range of family structures before comparison — use books, photographs and class sharing to build the range before moving to comparison.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Classroom diversity means family structures will vary significantly — authentic class-level sharing provides rich, relevant data for understanding contemporary variety.
success_criteria: Identifies at least three different family structures by name
Describes one similarity and one difference between two family structures

nodes.label: Roles of family members
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe roles played by different family members (parents, children, extended family) and note that these roles can vary across families.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least two different roles played by family members (e.g. caregiver, breadwinner, elder) and give an example of each.
nodes.typical_width: Examine roles of parents, children and extended family members across a range of family structures; note how roles can vary by culture, age and circumstance.
wider: Investigate how roles of elders and extended family members differ in First Nations Australian families compared with other family types
Explore how gender roles within families have changed across generations

response_modes.reason: Family roles are most effectively explored through comparison — use parent/grandparent interviews alongside class sharing to reveal the range.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The intersection of culture, gender and generation in family roles creates rich opportunities for comparative discussion that deepens historical thinking.
success_criteria: Names at least two roles played by family members
Notes that the same role can be filled by different people in different families

nodes.label: Change and continuity over time
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare family structures and roles from the past (parents' and grandparents' generations) with the present, identifying what has changed and what has remained the same.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare at least one family structure or role from a grandparent's time with today, identifying one change and one continuity.
nodes.typical_width: Compare family structures and roles across at least two generations using photographs, oral histories and discussions with family elders; identify patterns of change and continuity in family size, roles and composition.
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australian family and kinship structures have shown continuity despite the pressures of colonisation
Explore how immigration and migration patterns have changed family structures across generations in Australia

response_modes.reason: This node integrates knowledge of current structures (Node 1) and roles (Node 2) with historical comparison — the change/continuity analysis is the full descriptor demand.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one change in family structures or roles across generations
Identifies at least one aspect of family life that has remained the same over time
